$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-LIR-THREAD-LOCAL-IMPORT-STAMPED-READ-THROUGH-A-SLOT): a DSS unit that only DECLARES two thread-locals, defined by a reference compiler's archive member (quoted in main.c). MIR->LIR registered every data import as read through an address slot, a thread-local one included, so the import row left stamped `readThroughSlot`, the link minted an address slot for the definition and retargeted the thread-pointer access into it, and the ELF writer refused the image (K_RelocationKindMismatch) on both ELF execs, at HEAD 71648598 as in this round's tree. The references on THIS main.c and these archives (2026-10-07, WSL): gcc 13.3.0 + GNU ld 2.42, clang 18.1.3 + GNU ld and + ld.lld 18.1.3 at -O0 and -O2, and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu-aarch64 at -O0 and -O2: 42, 8 of 8. Two threads each see their OWN copies (the exit-code ladder is in main.c). The Mach-O and pe64 arms are absent because there the reference object's DEFINITION is refused at read (`__DATA,__thread_vars` / `.tls$` resolve to no section kind), a separate row; this example gains those arms when it closes.
